Which of these EU regulations apply to a manufacturer of connected robotic lawnmowers?
options: Radio Equipment Directive – cybersecurity delegated act
explanations: Yes – product with digital elements; vulnerability reporting since 11 Sep 2026.
Yes – the mower uses Wi-Fi/Bluetooth/cellular; applies since 1 Aug 2025.
Yes – the mower is machinery; applies from 20 Jan 2027, includes protection against corruption.
Yes – location data and garden maps are personal data.
It depends – manufacture of machinery (NACE C28) is in Annex II; applies if Lumion is medium-sized or larger.
It depends – only if AI is a safety component, e.g. vision-based obstacle detection.
No – DORA covers the financial sector.

questions.text: Stage 1: 40 customers report mowers starting at 3 a.m. and leaving the garden boundary. What is your FIRST action?
options: Send a notice to all customers
Contact the researcher who reported the flaw
explanations: Do this right after – logs are evidence.

questions.text: Stage 2: The vulnerability is actively exploited and customers' GPS data may be exposed. Whom must Lumion notify, and how fast?
options: National CSIRT and ENISA: early warning within 24 h (CRA); data protection authority within 72 h (GDPR)
No one until a fix exists

questions.text: Stage 3: The media asks for a comment and a hacktivist group claims responsibility. Who should speak?
options: The communications lead, with an agreed message

questions.text: Stage 4: A partly tested fix is ready, and the OTA signing key was stored in plain text in the CI pipeline. What do you do?
options: Keep mowers stopped and test first
Rotate the signing key first, then release
